classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `lib/Parser/JSLexer.cpp:956`. Source-grounded analysis shows the read happens because `consumeBracedCodePoint()` keeps iterating after `error()` has already forced EOF, then dereferences `curCharPtr_` one byte past the source buffer.

bug_description.original: A heap out of bounds read occurs in JSLexer::consumeBracedCodePoint due to continued use of the curCharPtr_ pointer after it is set to the end of the buffer. This situation arises when an invalid code point triggers a call to forceEOF in JSLexer::error, which sets curCharPtr_ to the buffer's end, but JSLexer::consumeBracedCodePoint does not properly handle this state and reads past the buffer boundary.
bug_description.normalized: When Hermes lexes the exact witness `\u{ `, `consumeBracedCodePoint()` sees the space after `{` as an invalid code-point character and calls `error()`. In the saved runtime, the first lexer error reaches the configured error limit, so `error()` calls `forceEOF()` and returns false. The invalid-character branch ignores that false return, continues the loop, advances `curCharPtr_` from `bufferEnd_` to `bufferEnd_ + 1`, and the next loop-condition read at line 956 performs the observed out-of-bounds read.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that consumes the fuzzed source bytes by dispatching a leading backslash token into Unicode-escape parsing.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 4 bytes `5C 75 7B 20` (`\u{ `). In the saved Stage 01 stack `JSParserImpl::parse()` calls `lexer_.advance()`, the first byte `0x5c` selects this backslash path, and the following bytes `u{` carry the lexer into `consumeBracedCodePoint()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Missing check of `error()`'s boolean return in the invalid-character arm. When the first lexer error reaches the configured error limit, `error()` forces EOF and returns false, but this caller still falls through to `continue` instead of aborting the braced-codepoint parse.
root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this exact site by returning immediately when `error()` returns false, preventing the later post-increment past `bufferEnd_`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The loop-condition dereference executes after the cursor has already been advanced to `bufferEnd_ + 1`, so it reads one byte past the source buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved AddressSanitizer report is `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `lib/Parser/JSLexer.cpp:956` with stack `consumeBracedCodePoint -> consumeUnicodeEscape -> advance`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness has already entered Hermes's JavaScript parser here; tokenization of the first source token begins when `lexer_.advance()` is called.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first payload byte after `{` is materialized as `ch`; for this witness it is ASCII space `0x20`, which is neither hex nor `}` and drives the invalid-character path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The fourth and final byte of the exact `poc` witness `5C 75 7B 20` (`\u{ `).
tainted_value_origin.note: By this point `consumeBracedCodePoint()` has already advanced past `{`, so `curCharPtr_` is reading the witness's trailing space.

fine_trace.note: Source. `advance()` is already in its backslash branch for the witness's first byte `0x5c`, and this call begins Unicode-escape parsing on attacker-controlled source text. The exact staged file is `\u{ `, so the lexer will next see `u{` followed by a space.

After consuming `\u`, this branch reads the next byte `{` and dispatches into `consumeBracedCodePoint()`. The witness has no closing `}` after this brace, so the braced-codepoint parser will examine the following space as its first payload byte.

The function has already advanced past `{`, so this statement reads the PoC's final byte `0x20` (space) into `ch`. It is neither hex nor `}`, and because the cursor is still before `bufferEnd_`, execution enters the invalid-character arm rather than the explicit EOF return.

The invalid-character arm calls `error()` on the space from step 3. In the saved runtime, `BCProviderFromSrc::createBCProviderFromSrc()` installs `SimpleDiagHandlerRAII`, which sets the error limit to 1, so this first lexer error reaches the limit: `forceEOF()` sets `curCharPtr_ = bufferEnd_` and `error()` returns false.

Root cause. This caller ignores the false return from step 4. Even after EOF has been forced, control falls through to `failed = true; continue;` instead of returning from `consumeBracedCodePoint()`. The staged patch adds that missing early return at this exact site.

Because step 5 executes `continue;` after step 4 forced EOF, the `for` header's post-increment still runs. That moves `curCharPtr_` from `bufferEnd_` to `bufferEnd_ + 1`, past the zero terminator that `initializeWithBufferId()` requires at `*bufferEnd_`.

Sink. The next iteration reevaluates `*curCharPtr_ != '}'` with `curCharPtr_ == bufferEnd_ + 1`, so the loop condition performs the observed 1-byte out-of-bounds read. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of a 32-byte region allocated here by `make_unique<StringBuffer>(s)`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes each `error(...)` site inside `consumeBracedCodePoint()` to return immediately when `error()` returns false, which prevents the post-EOF loop continuation and the subsequent line-956 dereference. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

format.name: raw JavaScript source
format.contract: Exactly the 4-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_23725/poc`: `5C 75 7B 20` (`\u{ `). Parsed as JavaScript source, the first token begins with a backslash, the next two bytes are `u{`, the first braced-codepoint payload byte is a space (not hex), and the file ends without any closing `}`. In the saved Stage 01 runtime, `SimpleDiagHandlerRAII` sets the lexer error limit to 1, so that first invalid-character diagnostic forces EOF; because the vulnerable code ignores the false return from `error()`, the lexer advances past `bufferEnd_` and the next line-956 loop-condition read crashes. The staged artifacts do not prove broader malformed braced escapes beyond this exact witness.
